objective: Re-confirm the SUE/PEAD construction and mechanism, and pin the 8-K Item-2.02 acceptance-timestamp semantics, before rebuilding the refuted pead_sue_eps_event card with visible_at moved to the 8-K announcement time.
existing_solution_comparison: SUE construction (Foster-Olsen-Shevlin 1984 seasonal random walk) and PEAD (Bernard-Thomas 1989) are unchanged, already implemented in scripts/build_sec_xbrl_fundamentals.py and reused verbatim. The only new work is the visible_at join to 8-K Item-2.02 acceptance timestamps, which are already collected locally (data/features/earnings_events/, built under docs/plan-earnings-text-forward-test-2026-09-22.zh.md T1). No new signal, admission rule, or cost convention is introduced.
negative_experiments_checked: dir:pead_xbrl_sue_filing_date (refuted): beats_redated=False and book_positive_20bp=False at the primary horizon under the 10-Q/10-K filing-date visible_at. This iteration changes only that one variable, per the card's own reopen note.

sources.core_claim: Systematic post-earnings-announcement drift in security returns is associated with the sign and magnitude of unexpected earnings (measured against a seasonal-random-walk expectation); for expectation models based on the time series of reported quarterly earnings, sign/magnitude of forecast error and firm size jointly explain 85% of the variation in drift; the drift is persistent 1974-1981, not concentrated in a subperiod.
sources.project_applicability: This is the exact SUE construction reused unchanged in scripts/build_sec_xbrl_fundamentals.py::sue_series (seasonal random walk on same-quarter-prior-year EPS differences) and in the refuted pead_sue_eps_event card; this iteration does not alter this construction, only the visible_at timestamp of the resulting event.
sources.reflection: Read via WebSearch result summary (Stanford GSB working-paper listing plus Semantic Scholar abstract); the original 1984 Accounting Review PDF is paywalled and was not independently opened this pass -- the abstract/summary is treated as reliable given it is corroborated across two independent listings (Stanford GSB, Semantic Scholar).

sources.core_claim: Post-earnings-announcement drift (Ball-Brown 1968's finding that cumulative abnormal returns keep drifting after the earnings announcement, up for good-news firms and down for bad-news firms) is examined to discriminate between a delayed price response and a risk-premium explanation.
sources.project_applicability: Names the phenomenon (drift AFTER the announcement) this project's pead_sue_eps_event card and this iteration's rebuild both test; directly supports the premise that the announcement event itself, not a later accounting filing, is the economically correct anchor for the drift window.
sources.reflection: Read via WebSearch result summary (RePEc/IDEAS listing, corroborated by JSTOR and Semantic Scholar listings); the original JAR 1989 PDF is paywalled and was not independently opened this pass.

sources.core_claim: Using actual quote data 1993-2002, an investor trading immediately on the earnings announcement (not waiting until market close) could have earned hedged-portfolio returns of at least 14%/yr after trading costs; the paper's title is literally 'Post-Earnings Announcement Drift: Timing and Liquidity Costs'.
sources.project_applicability: Directly on point: this is independent published evidence that WHEN you become able to act on the earnings surprise (announcement time vs. a later, coarser timestamp) is a first-order driver of whether PEAD survives costs -- exactly the single variable (visible_at) this iteration changes.
sources.reflection: Already verified in this repo (reports/harness/source_cards/profit_route_challenge_20260921.jsonl, claim_id pead_cost_counterpoint, fetched 2026-09-21) and reconfirmed live today (2026-09-28) via a fresh Crossref fetch of the same DOI record; title/authors/abstract match.

sources.core_claim: Transaction costs significantly reduce PEAD trading profits, and high gross excess returns tend to concentrate in high-transaction-cost stocks.
sources.project_applicability: The counterweight to battalio_mendenhall_2006: cost sensitivity is real and is exactly why this iteration keeps the project's own fixed 10/20bp cost convention unchanged rather than assuming the announcement-timing fix alone guarantees a profitable book.
sources.reflection: Already verified in this repo (reports/harness/source_cards/profit_route_challenge_20260921.jsonl, claim_id pead_cost_counterevidence, fetched 2026-09-21); not re-fetched today, cited for balance against the more favorable battalio_mendenhall_2006 finding.

sources.core_claim: Replicating classic SUE-based PEAD on US stock data Feb 2001-Dec 2024: all-stocks t-statistic 2.18 (barely significant), but dropping to 1.43 (not significant) once microcaps are excluded; the brief concludes 'the inclusion of the microcaps was the reason PEAD appeared'.
sources.project_applicability: Directly matches the caveat already carried in the refuted card's own rationale (reports/research/signal-cards/fundamentals-v1-manifest.json signal pead_sue_eps_event, same t=2.18/t=1.43 figures) -- confirms this iteration should treat any admission as a microcap-tilted, tier-1/2-scrutinized effect, not a durable large-cap anomaly, exactly as the prior card already flagged.
sources.reflection: Read via a live WebFetch today (2026-09-28) of the UCLA Anderson Review's own published brief; the brief summarizes Subrahmanyam's SSRN paper (papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5930255) which was not separately opened this pass -- the brief's direct quotes of the t-statistics are treated as a faithful secondary source, consistent with the number this repo already carried from a prior, independently-sourced reading.

sources.core_claim: Item 2.02 (Results of Operations and Financial Condition) requires disclosure, including the date and text (as an exhibit) of any public announcement or release of material non-public information about a completed quarterly or annual fiscal period's results of operations or financial condition; information furnished under Item 2.02 is 'furnished', not 'filed'. In practice the large majority of Item 2.02 8-Ks are earnings-release press statements furnished as Exhibit 99.
sources.project_applicability: Confirms the join target (8-K filings with Item 2.02) is specifically the earnings-release announcement event, the correct anchor for visible_at under the reopen condition; corroborates the existing local build (scripts/build_earnings_events.py REQUIRED_ITEM='2.02', EX-99 exhibit extraction) was built against the right SEC category.
sources.reflection: The PDF itself could not be machine-read this pass (binary/compressed stream, confirmed reachable via a live fetch today); the core claim above is taken from a corroborating WebSearch summary (sec-api.io's own description of the same Item 2.02 dataset) cross-checked against this project's own already-built and already-tested earnings_events pipeline, which independently encodes the same 'furnished, Exhibit 99, earnings release' pattern.

sources.core_claim: data.sec.gov provides public, no-authentication RESTful JSON APIs for company submissions and extracted XBRL data; the submissions endpoint returns each entity's filing history as a compact columnar data array.
sources.project_applicability: Confirms the base API this project's data/features/earnings_events table (and the fundamentals-v1 SEC XBRL build) is built against is the correct, current, official SEC access path -- no separate scraping or unofficial API is used for the 8-K timestamp join.
sources.reflection: Fetched live today (2026-09-28); this specific page's rendered text did not enumerate field names (acceptanceDateTime/accessionNumber/form/items) explicitly, so the field-level detail is corroborated instead by this repo's own already-built and spot-checked earnings_events pipeline (scripts/build_earnings_events.py docstring, which records that acceptanceDateTime/accessionNumber/form/items are the exact fields read from filings.recent, and that the Eastern-time-vs-UTC quirk in acceptanceDateTime was verified live during that build) rather than re-derived from this page alone.

sources.core_claim: Describes a commercial dataset of Form 8-K Item 2.02 earnings-results filings back to 2004, corroborating that Item 2.02 filings are the standard SEC-tracked category for earnings-release announcements.
sources.project_applicability: Independent (non-SEC) corroboration that Item 2.02 is the market-standard proxy for 'earnings announced', used only as a secondary check alongside the primary SEC source above, not as the basis for any construction detail.
sources.reflection: Read via WebSearch result snippet; not independently fetched in full, used only for corroboration, not as a load-bearing source.
